purpose: Make the branch feedback from lower 1942-43 net aircrew losses explicit: surviving experienced crews return as instructors/cadres, increasing conversion quality and recovery slope without inventing extra aircraft or fuel.

core_rule.do_not_model_as: historical replacement graduation + static attrition only
core_rule.model_as: new graduates + recovered wounded + rotated veterans + cadres from reorganized/disbanded units - combat/noncombat permanent losses, with cadre allocation modifying conversion speed and ready fraction
core_rule.nonlinearity: Preserved leaders/navigation/multi-seat crews allow new personnel to be embedded into mixed-experience units instead of rebuilding whole units from novices.

IJN_carrier_air.constraint: carrier landing qualification, deck-team integration and multi-carrier strike coordination remain narrow bottlenecks; secondary carriers absorb training/ferry/rear-CAP load.

reasons: natural rotation/recovery to home and rear training establishments
less need to rebuild units entirely from novice crews
IJN_land_based_air.constraint: fuel, type conversion, long-range navigation/torpedo specialization and airframe supply still cap output.

reasons: large historical training establishment already exists
no U-Go avoids a major 1944 Burma aircrew/airframe sink and reduces emergency front absorption
IJA_land_based_air.constraint: fuel, serviceability, modern-type availability, maintenance and theater transport; this is not a 15-30% increase in factory production.

allocation_rule: The multiplier applies to the rate at which assigned aircraft become crewed/mission-ready and to replacement sustainability. It must not be applied again to raw aircraft production, physical OOB, or a theater band that already explicitly includes the same regeneration effect.
Bengal_implication: The earlier 5th Air Division 135-180 whole-theater / 70-105 western-subset bands were too conservative once branch survival and no-U-Go retention are combined. Use the v003 Indian Ocean air ledger instead.
strategic_implication: Time has higher option value for Japan than in a static historical replacement model. Two to four weeks of protected training/regeneration can materially improve unit cohesion even when nominal aircraft count changes little.
